name: echo
description: Prints text or variable values to standard output.

flags.description: Interpret escape sequences: \n newline, \t tab, \\ backslash.
Do not print the trailing newline.
Single quotes prevent expansion — the literal text is printed.

examples.explanation: Double quotes expand variables. If your login is user, it prints Hello, user.
Single quotes print everything literally — no expansion happens.
Appends a line to your shell config — the standard way to persist settings.

about: echo is a shell builtin. Quoting rules matter more than the command itself: double quotes expand variables and keep spaces together; single quotes are fully literal; no quotes lets the shell split on whitespace and expand globs. For portable scripts, printf is more predictable.
mistakes: echo $VAR without quotes — word splitting and glob expansion can corrupt the value; use echo "$VAR".
Relying on \n without -e — many shells print it literally.
warnings: Different shells' echo handle -e and -n inconsistently; printf is the portable choice for scripts.
